name: Nimrod
description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs

points: Cush begat Nimrod: these are Hamites. He began to be a mighty one in the earth: a leader, an elite leader, and evil as hell also. He was a mighty hunter before the Lord: he hunted after men; a man of the field too also. When it says mighty hunter, it means he was very evil, an evil leader or ruler.

In ancient archaeology, the white man doesn't want to know this, so he hides this history, because if you prove that Nimrod existed, the Bible's given validation. The first king of Babylon was known as Sargon of Akkad, recognized to be one of the first rulers of this kingdom of Babylonia; Sargon means King of Akkad, the Akkadians. That's Nimrod. And when he died, they deified him as a god.

note.label: As in the Days of Noah: Past & Present

points: And Cush begat Nimrod: he began to be a mighty one in the earth, a mighty hunter before the Lord, meaning he was against the Lord. The beginning of his kingdom was Babel in the land of Shinar. So after the flood, the first empire was Kush: the Ethiopians, the Sudan. These were mighty men with understanding. You look at these Discovery Channel programs and they have white people as the first empire; no, the Bible says the children of Ham were the first ruling empire on the earth after the flood. Before the flood, Cain built the first city.
Cush begat Nimrod: this is what we wanted to get to.
I want you to remember that name Nimrod, who was the son of Cush, an Ethiopian.

note.label: The Truth Behind Christmas and New Years

points: When it says consensus view, that means modern scholarship. Real scholars will tell you the best books to have are the oldest ones, because they go back closer to that time. Modern scholars, a lot of them are secular or atheists, and they'll come behind those old scholars and go, they were wrong; that was their opinion; to remove any Bible validation whatsoever. But it is true: Cain did build in that area, and Nimrod built on top of that. That's where the evil was. That's why the Lord told Abraham to move from there, to leave there, cuz it was so evil.

note.label: As in the Days of Noah: Past & Present

points: Israel captive in Babylon, past, present and future: ancient Babylon under Nimrod, neo-Babylon under Nebuchadnezzar, and today. “He was a mighty hunter before the Lord”: he hunted the souls of men. He got them all together and had everybody follow his one world religion; everybody followed it, and they all got together to build that tower.

note.label: | SABBATH EVENING CLASS: The Third Kingdom of Babylon

points: “And the land of Nimrod”: the land of Nimrod is Babylon, and that is this place right here, America. So we are hitting them on two fronts with the Bible, the word of God: we’re getting them over there and we’re getting them over here.

We went through all of that, the burden of Babylon, the warning to the teachers and the parable of the fig tree, to explain this verse. “And they shall waste the land of Assyria with the sword, and the land of Nimrod in the entrances thereof” means we are going to use the word of God as our sword, and we are going to teach and preach and shake kingdoms.
“And they shall waste the land of Assyria with the sword”: the sword is the word of God. “And the land of Nimrod”: that’s Babylon the great. Remember Nimrod’s kingdom was called Babel.
